sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/tabor-campground ('It has 15 sites and accommodates large recreational vehicles'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: No water at the campground in 2026; the RV dump stations at Printer Boy and White Star campgrounds are closed this season too. Firewood sold at the host site.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10165686 (notice 'Water will NOT be available in this campground in 2026 ... the RV Dump Stations at both Printer Boy & White Star Campgrounds will remain closed this season'; 'Facilities include picnic tables, fire rings with grates, and a vault toilet') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/tabor-campground ('A vault toilet is available'; 'Potable water is not available at this site'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: $29 a site per night, two vehicles or one RV included; third vehicle $11 a night; overflow parking $25 a night. Recreation.gov's first-come season tables show the same $29 for 2026 and 2027.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/tabor-campground ('$29 fee per site for overnight camping. Two vehicles or one recreational vehicle is included in camping fee. $11 fee for a third vehicle'; '$25 fee for overflow parking per night') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10165686/rates (First-come, First-served Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-06 and 2027-05-21 to 2027-09-05: WalkInScanPay1 $29), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Strictly first come, first served: arrive to claim a site, pay at the self-service fee tube (cash, check or money order) or by recreation.gov Scan & Pay on site. Sites must be occupied the first night.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/tabor-campground ('This campground is strictly first come, first served. Visitors are required to physically arrive at the campground to purchase and claim a site'; 'A self-service fee tube is available for on-site payment. First-come, first-served sites must be occupied the first night.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10165686 ('available on a first-come, first-served basis only'; rule scanAndPay 'S&P Only'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: May to September per the Forest Service, weather dependent; recreation.gov's first-come season runs May 22 - Sep 6 in 2026 and May 21 - Sep 5 in 2027.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/tabor-campground ('Seasons of Use: May to September. Opening and closing dates are weather dependent.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10165686/rates (First-come, First-served Season dates), read 2026-10-28

note: Set back in lodgepole on the northeast shore of Turquoise Lake, ~9,900 ft; Leadville RD. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov (10165686) API/rates: confirmed 15 sites, vault toilet, no water in 2026 (rec.gov notice dated for 2026; the FS page still says 2025), $29 (2026 and 2027), strictly FCFS; added season May-Sept, booking detail (Scan & Pay, fee tube). Note cleaned of field facts. Pin fine. Website should be the FS campground page, not the forest home page.
flags: Website: stored https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc is the forest home page. Use the campground's own page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/tabor-campground (and recreation.gov https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/10165686, first-come Scan & Pay listing).

Phone: none stored. Leadville Ranger District 719-486-0749 (FS Tabor page, Office Contact Information). recreation.gov's facility line (661) 702-1420 and contact email @goexplorus.com are the concessionaire's (Explorus), not the district's. Suggest 719-486-0749.
Operator: a concessionaire (recreation.gov contact tbolton@goexplorus.com; the FS page's pass text refers to 'concessionaire-run campsites'). Ownership federal stands.

Water 2026 confirmed and dated: recreation.gov notice 'Water will NOT be available in this campground in 2026 ... the RV Dump Stations at both Printer Boy & White Star Campgrounds will remain closed this season.' The FS page still carries the 2025 version ('Water will not be available in this campground in 2025') and its description still lists 'potable water'.

Length: no figure anywhere; FS and recreation.gov both say it 'accommodates large recreational vehicles', and the rec.gov per-site catalog has a single placeholder site with no attributes. 'All vehicles must fit in the parking spur.' No criteria problem.

Pin: stored 39.27539,-106.35707 is the FS/rec.gov facility point, on the north edge of the upper paved lot by the shore (imagery shows RVs parked along it). The rec.gov catalog has no per-site coordinates (one placeholder site at the same point). Kept.

Road: FS alert (April 7, 2026, still open-ended) 'Turquoise Lake Road (County Road 4) has been closed due to asphalt damage. The road is barricaded from the Abe Lee parking turnoff to Hagerman Pass. Access to Turquoise Lake is still available via County Road 9C and County Road 9 to the Hagerman Pass intersection.' Tabor is on the northeast shore toward the Leadville end, which appears to be outside the barricaded section; not confirmed on a map. No closure of the campground itself.

Waterfront (stored lakeview, kept): on imagery the campground's paved lot at the pin sits ~50-70 m back from the lake's high-water edge (the top of the exposed drawdown beach), with a continuous band of lodgepole and a second (lower) paved lot between it and the shore; the lower lot opens to the beach at its west end. That buffer rules out lakefront; the view through the trees is partial, so lakeview is the most it earns (not waterfront would also be defensible). The imagery is undated and shows a wide drawn-down beach; I found no published 2026 lake level, so the 2026 check could not be done.
